facts.statement: The fossil remains of Notocolossus were discovered in Mendoza province by Argentine paleontologist Dr. Bernardo Javier González Riga.
facts.quote: A fossil of a large sauropod was discovered by the Argentine paleontologist Dr. Bernardo Javier González Riga in Mendoza province.

facts.statement: The species Notocolossus gonzalezparejasi was formally named and described in 2016 by a team led by Bernardo Javier González Riga.
facts.quote: In 2016, the type species Notocolossus gonzalezparejasi was named and described by Bernardo Javier González Riga, Matthew Carl Lamanna, Leonardo Daniel Ortiz David, Jorge Orlando Calvo and Juan P. Coria.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton is incomplete, lacking the skull but including vertebrae, a humerus, and part of a pubic bone.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull. It contains an anterior back vertebra, an anterior tail vertebra, a right humerus and the upper part of a left pubic bone.

facts.statement: A second, smaller partial skeleton was assigned to the genus Notocolossus.
facts.quote: A second partial skeleton lacking the skull was referred to Notocolossus: specimen UNCUYO-LD 302 representing a smaller individual.

facts.statement: Notocolossus held the record for the largest Cretaceous sauropod humerus until 2026, when a larger one was found in Nagatitan.
facts.quote: It held the record for the largest humerus preserved for any Cretaceous sauropod until the description of Nagatitan in 2026 with its 1.78 m humerus.

facts.statement: Scientists estimated the total femur length of Notocolossus to be 2.166 meters.
facts.quote: They also estimated the total femur length at 2.166 m, by using an allometric equation.

facts.statement: Based on body proportions, Notocolossus likely weighed between 44.9 and 75.9 tonnes, with 60.4 tonnes being the most probable estimate.
facts.quote: If, as is likely, the body proportions of Notocolossus were comparable to those of better preserved titanosaurs, the new dinosaur may have weighed in the range of 44.9 - 75.9 t, most likely 60.4 t.

facts.statement: Researchers identified nine unique derived traits, or autapomorphies, specific to Notocolossus.
facts.quote: Nine of these were autapomorphies, unique derived qualities.

facts.statement: Vertical ridges on the front tail vertebrae fuse at their lower ends to form a V-shaped structure.
facts.quote: On the front side of the neural spines of the front tail vertebrae, run vertical ridges fusing at their lower ends, above the level of the front joint processes, creating a V-shaped structure.

facts.statement: The upper edge of the humerus is 2.9 times wider than the shaft diameter.
facts.quote: The humerus has in general a strongly expanded upper edge, 2.9 wider than the shaft diameter.

facts.statement: The upper width of the first metatarsal exceeds its length.
facts.quote: The first metatarsal has an upper width exceeding its length.

facts.statement: The toe claws of Notocolossus are reduced, rough, and truncated.
facts.quote: The toe claws are reduced, rough and truncated.

facts.statement: The foot of Notocolossus displays a unique build that is rarely preserved in sauropods.
facts.quote: The foot or pes of Notocolossus, a skeleton part that is not often preserved in sauropods, shows a unique build.

facts.statement: Notocolossus presents truncated unguals, a characteristic otherwise unknown in Sauropoda.
facts.quote: It also presents truncated unguals, characteristics otherwise unknown in the Sauropoda.

facts.statement: A 2017 study placed Notocolossus outside of Lithostrotia as the sister taxon of Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: A 2017 study by Carballido and colleagues recovered it as the sister taxon of Lognkosauria and found it to be outside of Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: A 2018 study placed Notocolossus within Lognkosauria in a polytomy with Patagotitan and Puertasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2018, González Riga and colleagues found it to belong to Lognkosauria, in a polytomy with Patagotitan and Puertasaurus.

facts.statement: Notocolossus lived during the late Cretaceous in Mendoza Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Notocolossus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from late Cretaceous strata of Mendoza Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Notocolossus lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, 86 million years ago, in what is now Argentina.
facts.quote: Notocolossus es un saurópodo titanosaurio que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 86 millones de años, en lo que ahora es Argentina.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Notocolossus was among the largest titanosaurs and one of the heaviest land animals ever discovered.
facts.quote: The evidence suggests that Notocolossus was among the largest titanosaurs, and therefore one of the heaviest land animals, yet discovered.

facts.statement: The ecosystem of the Plottier Formation included mammals, a large coelurosaur, and several titanosaur species.
facts.quote: Tetrapods of the Plottier formation are poorly known. They are represented by mammals, a large coelurosaur, and several titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Notocolossus is estimated to have weighed between 44.9 and 60.4 tonnes and measured between 25 and 32 meters in length.
facts.quote: Algunas estimaciones indican que Notocolossus podría haber tenido un peso entre 44,9 y 60,4 toneladas, y una longitud de entre 25 y 32 metros.

facts.statement: The humerus of Notocolossus measures 1.76 meters, making it longer than the known humerus of any other titanosaurian.
facts.quote: su húmero o hueso del brazo superior tiene 1,76 metros de longitud, que es más largo que el de cualquier otro titanosauriano por el cual se conoce este hueso

facts.statement: The foot claws of Notocolossus are reduced, blunt, and truncated, a feature unknown among other sauropods.
facts.quote: Las garras del pie son reducidas, romas y truncadas.

facts.statement: Fossils of Notocolossus were discovered by Argentine paleontologist Dr. Bernardo Javier González Riga in Mendoza Province and published in 2016.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Notocolossus fueron descubiertos por el paleontólogo argentino Dr. Bernardo Javier González Riga en la provincia de Mendoza y publicados en el año 2016

facts.statement: The genus name Notocolossus combines Greek words for "south" and "giant statue," referencing the animal's Southern Hemisphere origin and massive size.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina las palabras griegas νότος, notos, "sur", y κολοσσός, kolossos, "coloso", "estatua gigante", en referencia a la procedencia del animal del hemisferio sur y su tamaño gigantesco.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UNCUYO-LD 301 was found in strata of the Plottier Formation dating from the Coniacian to Santonian ages.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, UNCUYO-LD 301, fue hallado en estratos de la Formación Plottier, de edad desde el Coniaciense - Santoniense.

facts.statement: Although the bones were not articulated, they were considered to belong to a single individual because they were found in close association on an eight-by-eight meter surface.
facts.quote: Aunque los huesos no se han descubierto en la articulación, se consideró que representaban a un solo individuo porque se encontraron en estrecha asociación en una superficie de ocho por ocho metros.

facts.statement: A second specimen, UNCUYO-LD 302, represents a smaller individual with five anterior caudal vertebrae and a complete, articulated foot, an exceptional find for any sauropod.
facts.quote: Se asocian a otro ejemplar, UNCUYO-LD 302, que representa un individuo más pequeño representado por una serie de cinco vértebras caudales anteriores, y un pie completo y articulado, hallazgo excepcional para cualquier saurópodo.

facts.statement: A 2016 cladistic analysis placed Notocolossus within Titanosauria, in the group Lithostrotia, as a basal taxon sister to Dreadnoughtus.
facts.quote: En el estudio de 2016, se incluyó un análisis cladístico en que se situó a Notocolossus dentro de Titanosauria, en el grupo Lithostrotia, en una posición relativamente basal como un taxón hermano de Dreadnoughtus.

facts.statement: In 2018, González Riga and colleagues determined that Notocolossus belonged to Lognkosauria, in a polytomy with Patagotitan and Puertasaurus.
facts.quote: En 2018, González Riga y sus colegas descubrieron que pertenecía a Lognkosauria, en una politomía con Patagotitan y Puertasaurus.

facts.statement: Notocolossus lived from the Coniacian to the Santonian, approximately 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tetrapods from the Plottier Formation are poorly known and include mammals, a large ceratosaurian, and several titanosaurians.
facts.quote: Los tetrápodos de la formación Plottier son poco conocidos. Están representados por mamíferos , un gran celurosaurio y varios titanosaurianos.

facts.statement: Nine distinct derived features were identified as autapomorphies unique to Notocolossus.
facts.quote: Nueve de estos eran autapomorfias, o características únicas derivadas.

facts.statement: The foot of Notocolossus shows a unique constitution, as this part of the skeleton is rarely preserved in sauropods.
facts.quote: El pie de Notocolossus, una parte del esqueleto que no se preserva con frecuencia en los saurópodos, muestra una constitución única.

facts.statement: Notocolossus possessed a compact and homogeneous metatarsus, believed to be adapted to support its extraordinary weight.
facts.quote: Posee un metatarso compacto y homogéneo, que se cree estaba adaptado a sostener su extraordinario peso.
